description: A new session on a day whose tracker holds sixty tasks with paragraph-long items. Resume reads it through a `chief-of-stuff tracker` subcommand, never with grep, sed, awk, cat, head, tail or cut on the tracker file, and still reports what the `## Resume` block says (#46). The shell grader models what a coordinator writes and is not a shell parser: it fails a Bash call that names the tracker file (`tracker.md`, or a glob such as `*-tracker*`, `*tracker*`, `<date>-tracker*`) and runs one of those tools as a command word: first in the call; after `;`, `&`, `|`, `(`, a backtick, `{`, `!`, a newline or a tab; after do, then, else, if, while, until, command, env, time, eval, exec (and so `-exec`) or xargs with its flags; with or without `VAR=value` prefixes or a path to the tool. So a call that names the tracker file and pipes anything into one of the tools fails too. Not covered: `bash -c '…'`, a directory-wide `cat daily/*`, and a file name assembled from shell variables.

graders.name: tracker read through a tracker subcommand
no shell text tool on the tracker file
no Grep on the tracker file
reply names what was in flight
